name: welcome
body:
Hello ,  

Welcome to Capstone (D424)! Congrats on making it this far into your degree plan. My goal is to help guide you past this last hurdle and on to graduation!  Please read this email carefully before you start. Not doing so can slow down your progress and make the course more difficult.

 

DO NOT USE THE APPROVAL FORM IN THE COURSE . Please use the one from the SharePoint site linked in step # 1 below. Using the form found in the course itself may delay your project being approved because it doesn't contain all the necessary fields for an instructor to approve your project.

Even though the generic welcome email says you need to make an appointment, it is not necessary.

 

FIRST STEPS:

  1. Visit D424 Course Resource for detailed explanations of tasks, templates, and sample papers. Bookmark this resource and use it every step of the way. You must read. Watching videos only will guarantee you miss important information. Videos are meant as a general explanation only.
  2. Check the Course of Study to see if any cohorts are available.
  3. Pick a project and submit your form for Task 1. Do not start Task 2 until Task 1 has passed.

 

RELEASE FORM:

You do not need a release form unless you are using code you developed for an employer or client. If you submit a release form, please make sure you check the appropriate box on the form.

 

Why Use the SharePoint Resource?

The Resources in the SharePoint above explains what the rubric means in detail, and includes templates and sample papers. There are known issues with how the tasks are written. I explain everything you need to pass in the SharePoint resource.

 

 Project Requirements:

  • App Type: Your application must be a full-stack web app or a mobile app. Desktop apps are not allowed. On the linked site above, I have a tutorial for C# students who may want to transition their desktop app to a .NET MVC Razor app. You'll find it on the page for Task 1.
  • Hosting: Your application must be hosted in the cloud.
  • Object-Oriented Concepts: Include key concepts like inheritance, polymorphism, and encapsulation. If you select a procedural language, emulate these concepts.
  • Task 3, Section B: Review this section carefully to ensure your app includes every required element.

 

NOTE: If you plan on submitting a mobile app, please pay close attention to the resource link below, particularly the page on that site regarding hosting. We do NOT recommend Google Play store.

 

IMPORTANT:

If you need a phone call: If you need a phone call and can't find time on my calendar, let me know. I work Sunday through Thursday each week, and depending on the day, I can usually fit you in the same day or the next day.

Please let me know if you have any questions. I'm here to help!
